items.title: Magic: The Gathering Returns to Marvel with Darkhold Destiny
items.excerpt: Magic the Gathering and Marvel have already crossed over a couple of times with Spider-Man and the Marvel Super Heroes set last year. But for its third Marvel set, MTG is getting spooky with Darkhold Destiny.
items.content_text: Magic: The Gathering and Marvel have already crossed over a couple of times with Spider-Man and the Marvel Super Heroes set last year. But for its third Marvel set, MTG is getting spooky with Darkhold Destiny. Rather than being based in a fairly mundane version of New York, Darkhold Destiny is taking the likes of Doctor Strange and the Asgardians and telling a more magical story (forgive me). What really separates this new out-there set from the other two Marvel sets is that Wizards of the Coast was really able to write its own story with Marvel's characters and settings, which makes them feel less like a crossover and more like a part of Magic's multiverse. With a new story written in-house, Wizards of the Coast was also able to give its artists more license to create their own takes on Marvel characters. For instance, with Scarlet Witch in the Marvel Super Heroes set, she looks like a pretty standard take on her comic book appearance. But in the art I was shown for Darkhold Destiny, she looks much more like an MTG character, while still retaining some of the signature parts of her outfit – the mask is still there. I was also given broad strokes of what the story is about. Essentially, Dormammu and Hela use the Darkhold to invade the entire multiverse, and it's up to Doctor Strange, Thor, and other Marvel heroes to stop them. Of course, because of the characters and, well, props that the story revolves around, the set is focused heavily on spellcasting. Thematically, the spellcasting is focused on what's essentially three different 'schools' of magic: Arcane, Divine, and Dark. Arcane magic will be themed around Doctor Strange and his allies, while Divine magic will be wielded by the Asgardians and other similar... entities. Dark magic is primarily going to be wielded by the villains of the set, but there are some heroes, like Ghost Rider that will apparently be wielding Dark magic. You can expect a lot of focus on cool instants, sorceries and 'unique enchantments.' Wizards is even bringing back the Arcane subtype on instants and sorceries, which hasn't been used since Saviors of Kamigawa all the way back in 2005. I even asked if WotC is bringing back the obscure 'Splice Onto Arcane' ability that let you combine different arcane spells, but sadly, it is not. Just like any other recent set, there will be a whole lineup of different Darkhold Destiny products. The standard fare is all here, Booster Packs, Collector Boosters and Bundles; but there will also be four commander decks. Strange Academy (White/Blue/Black) Gods of Asgard (White/Red/Green) Midnight Sons (White/Black) Lords of Hel (Black/Red) Each of these commander decks will also have a collector's edition available, which will be completely decked out in foils. There will also be two scene boxes, each with six mechanically unique cards. Both the Bundle and the special Gift Bundle will also come with a mechanically unique promo card, and I just hope they don't skyrocket immediately on TCGPlayer, but I know that they probably will. Wizards of the Coast will be giving the first glimpse of its original Marvel story in February with a comic produced alongside Image comics. Then, another comic will come out closer to when the set launches in April 2027.
items.title_en: Magic: The Gathering Returns to Marvel with Darkhold Destiny

items.title: GTA 6 Fan Says Rockstar Sent Them a Poster Just Because They Asked Nicely
items.excerpt: A Grand Theft Auto 6 fan in Brazil said they politely asked the Rockstar Games team to send them a poster – and it looks like they actually followed through.
items.content_text: A Grand Theft Auto 6 fan in Brazil said they politely asked the Rockstar Games team to send them a poster – and it looks like they actually followed through. Reddit user aogustoo shared their story in a post late last month. What began as a "shot-in-the-dark email" they sent to Rockstar asking for a signed GTA 6 poster has turned into what seems to be a heartwarming moment for them and the community. "A while ago I took a complete shot in the dark and emailed Rockstar," they said. "I shared how hyped I was for GTA VI and asked if there was any chance I could get a poster for my room. I sent a shot-in-the-dark email to Rockstar Games asking for a GTA VI poster, and they actually shipped one from their NYC office! by u/aogustoo in GTA6unmoderated "Honestly, I expected an automated reply or nothing at all. To my absolute surprise, an executive actually answered and shipped an official GTA VI poster straight from their New York office to my home in Brazil." You can see images, which show not only the poster but the emails they supposedly sent to receive it, above. As Rockstar (and the rest of the world) count down the days to GTA 6's November 19 launch, fans will no doubt be on the lookout for official merchandise like this. As many have pointed out, it's unclear if Rockstar truly took the time to send the poster, but the community is still looking to the moment as something worth celebrating as the countdown continues. "This is a massive W tho," Rockstar content creator @videotech said on X/Twitter . "This guy isn’t an influencer or someone famous, literally just a random Rockstar fan. Very kind of Rockstar and Take-Two to take the time and effort to do this." Comment by u/aogustoo from discussion in GTA6unmoderated "​I blurred out all personal addresses, names, and contact emails to respect their privacy," aogustoo added. "Please don't flood their inbox with requests, as I'm pretty sure this was just a rare act of kindness from someone on their team." There's still so much about GTA 6 that we don’t know, but one thing is for sure: Rockstar will probably get even more emails after this. While we wait to learn more about the next Grand Theft Auto game ahead of its November 19 launch for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S, you can check out IGN's recent interview with Rockstar North's Rob Nelson . You can also read about what Nintendo had to say about the chances of seeing GTA 6 on Switch 2 , some recently revealed radio stations , and even a batch of new screenshots .

items.title: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation: I Played a New Slice from the Early Game With a Boss Fight | IGN Preview
items.excerpt: While our earlier previews described a giant open-world game absolutely chock-full of activities, it was nice to see that the story-intense linear bits are still there, and just as dramatic as they were in the first two games. Final Fantasy VII Revelation will ultimately be the conclusion to this massive remake trilogy, and I can just tell that some of the content that was maybe a bit rushed in the original PlayStation game is going to be massive.
items.content_text: Key Preview Takeaways: Previous previews have focused on the open world, but my slice was focused on the more linear, story-intensive sections. Materia has a new way to level up. Difficulty was a bit lacking in this demo, but then again it was the first chapter of the game... We’re about six months out from Final Fantasy VII Revelation, and while that doesn’t seem like a huge wait, the anticipation to play the final chapter of the FF7 remake is palpable, especially since the first chapter dropped six(!) years ago now. We’ve also had the chance to go hands-on with Revelation before, and while the first couple previews were focused on flying around the open world in the Highwind, I got to play a much more linear slice at New York Comic Con. My demo opened up early in Chapter 1, when the party arrives at the North Crater, and it starts a linear path to the center of the giant hole. In both of the previews we’ve done already, IGN’s Michael Higham and Logan Plant both described Final Fantasy VII Revelation as this massive and overwhelming experience, but this first chapter felt more like walking into a late-game dungeon to fight a massive boss. Even my party members felt like late-game versions of themselves, fully decked out in Materia and equipment. But it’s important to keep in mind that this is just an early demo, so the balance could totally change before Revelation comes out in April. Both Remake and Rebirth looked incredible, and so does Revelation so far. But before I actually started wandering into the depths of the crater, I couldn’t help myself in digging through the menus a bit – after all, that’s half the fun of RPGs, right? Clicking into the Materia menu, there’s actually a new way you can level it up, rather than slowly absorbing AP as you kill stuff. There are now Materia fragments, each of which you can consume to add one AP ratio to your Materia. The remake’s third part didn’t really explain how I was supposed to gather these fragments, but I did start with 200 of them, so I just shoved all of them into my Fire Materia, which got it about a third of a level. I’m not sure I’d just dump them willy-nilly like that in the full game, because I’m not sure how rare they’ll be, but in a short 30-minute demo, what do I have to lose? The Item Transmuter has also returned from Rebirth, but crucially, gathering the materials for it should be much less of a pain. The auto-loot option that, for some reason, you had to beat the campaign to unlock in Rebirth is just enabled by default in Revelation. I was able to just run through the level and hoover up crafting materials without mashing the triangle button. That’s a huge improvement. After I was done poking around in the menus, I started to dive deeper into the crater, and it was gorgeous. Regardless of what I’m playing, there’s just something about levels with ice and crystals that always blows my mind, and delving through this crystalline labyrinth never ceases to amaze me – and I wasn’t even playing on the ‘Graphics’ optimization mode. Both Remake and Rebirth looked incredible, though, so it’s not surprising that Revelation is carrying that forward. But even though I was wandering starstruck through the crater, it wasn’t long before I ran into a group of monsters. The default party in the demo was Cloud, Cid, and Vincent, and of course I immediately swapped over to the new characters to see how they play. Cid immediately stood out. He has this rhythmic quality to his combat, where after one or two standard attacks, you wait for him to be wrapped in this weird blue mist, and then attack again to unleash a stronger attack. And those stronger attacks seem really strong, staggering a standard enemy almost immediately. I’ve already written about how Game Director Naoki Hamaguchi is going to make the platinum trophy easier to unlock . And it seems like that approach has carried over to combat. I was able to just melt through standard enemies without much thought. There were even larger enemies that spawned in with little mini-cutscenes, and I was able to dispatch them with just a couple of ATB abilities. Again, this is the first chapter, so it’s a little early to really get a feeling for how difficult the game will be when it opens up. Game Director Naoki Hamaguchi is going to make the platinum trophy easier to unlock. And it seems like that approach has carried over to combat. That difficulty (or lack thereof) made testing the new FITS system tricky. I wasn’t able to move FITS jobs around, but Cloud was assigned the Summoner job, and at the cost of one segment of the ATB meter, I was able to summon Ifrit, Shiva, or Titan to enhance my attacks. It was cool seeing some of my attacks land with explosions of fire or ice, but the real draw to this job, in my eyes, is the Synergy attacks each summon has. Synergy attacks work just like they do in Rebirth and Remake, where you have to use abilities to fill up a little bar. Use enough of them on specific characters and you unlock powerful abilities. The appeal to the summons’ synergy attacks, though, is that I only had to build up ATB on one character to use them, which should make it a lot easier to just churn through them. But most enemies died before I was able to use enough abilities to get to the Synergy ability. As I get deeper into the crater, I start running into Sephiroth clones – a ton of them – until Cloud has one of his signature visions of Sephiroth. I won’t go into too much detail on the particular nature of Sephiroth’s taunts here in the crater, but if you’ve played Final Fantasy VII on the PS1, you probably have a pretty good idea of what he’s saying. Eventually, creatures start fusing with the Sephiroth clones to create even more monstrous enemies, until I end up face-to-face with Gigas. And, unlike a lot of the smaller enemies before this, I was able to work up to one of Cloud’s synergy attacks with Ifrit, which ended up being a sort of fusion of the summon’s classic Hellfire attack with Cloud’s sword. However, before the animation finished, Gigas died. But, you know, we’re getting there. After facing a couple of subsequent enemies, I finally got to a whole crowd of Sephiroth clones surrounding a purple glow of some sort. A cutscene played, and, again, I’ll spare you the details, but it ended with Jenova Deathmourner hatching from one of the clones. Finally, something that can actually put up a fight! The boss fight plays out pretty similarly to other Jenova battles throughout the series, only this time the tentacles that spawn and make the boss invincible breathe fire. The fight is comprised of three phases, and so I was finally able to actually use multiple synergy abilities – Cid and Vincent, along with Cloud and Shiva. And they’re just as bombastic as they are in Rebirth. Eventually, after three phases of dodging fire and chopping down tentacles, the boss died and the demo was over. I would have liked the combat to be a bit more difficult, but it is still very early in the game, and there is likely going to be a lot of balance tuning as Final Fantasy VII Revelation gets closer to launch. Finally, while our earlier previews described a giant open-world game absolutely chock-full of activities, it was nice to see that the story-intense linear bits are still there, and just as dramatic as they were in the first two games. Final Fantasy VII Revelation will ultimately be the conclusion to this massive remake trilogy, and I can just tell that some of the content that was maybe a bit rushed in the original PlayStation game is going to be massive. items.title: Konami Planning 'Second and Third Waves' of New Silent Hill Games
items.excerpt: Konami is planning "second and third waves" of new Silent Hill games, according to producer Motoi Okamoto.
items.content_text: Konami is planning "second and third waves" of new Silent Hill games, according to producer Motoi Okamoto. Okamoto offered a foggy glimpse into the classic horror franchise's future during an interview featured in Famitsu Issue 1965 (via Game Observer ). The series ended a long, painful drought without new games with an initial wave of new releases over the last few years, and now that this first batch is out, Konami is already looking forward to what it can do next. "All three titles we initially announced were able to be released successfully, so we’re relieved (laughs)," he noted. "They’ve also received high praise, and we are satisfied with it." Okamoto continued: "Successfully launching this 'first wave' comes with great relief, but we’re not stopping here; we must think of the second and third waves. We can’t share specific details, but we’re currently looking at a number of projects." The first wave of Konami's return to Silent Hill – which included titles like the Silent Hill 2 remake , Silent Hill f , and last month's Silent Hill: Townfall – rolled out throughout the last few years. Townfall arrived as the most recent installment when it dropped players into the shoes of protagonist Simon Ordell in a '90s Scotland just last month. It received generally favorable reviews, with IGN giving it an 8/10 . We said, "Like the intravenous needle permanently jutting out of its hero’s wrist, Silent Hill: Townfall gives this long running series a welcome shot in the arm." It's a successful run of games that Konami is happy with, but getting here wasn't easy. After Hideo Kojima's Silent Hills failed to materialize, Okamoto said he had a hard time convincing higher-ups that more games was the way to go. However, as far as he was concerned, "just one remake is not enough," adding, "as a producer, I cannot let it end only with that." "If there were only one release, wouldn’t people think that the development is going to be cancelled again, I thought," Okamoto added. While Konami's plan to launch additional waves of Silent Hill games spells a promising future for fans who have missed the franchise, we have known that the series would continue in some form. Bloober Team, the horror-centric developer responsible for the Silent Hill 2 remake, confirmed it was working on a remake of the original Silent Hill last year.
items.title_en: Konami Planning 'Second and Third Waves' of New Silent Hill Games

items.title: Blumhouse Partners With MatPat to Make Amanda the Adventurer Movie, Confirms More Indie Horror Game Adaptations Are Coming | NYCC 2026
items.excerpt: Blumhouse Productions has partnered with YouTube star Matthew ‘MatPat’ Patrick to create a series of movies based on viral indie horror games, and Amanda the Adventurer is first on the docket.
items.content_text: Blumhouse Productions has partnered with YouTube star Matthew ‘MatPat’ Patrick to create a series of movies based on viral indie horror games, and Amanda the Adventurer is first on the docket. Representatives from Blumhouse and MatPat confirmed this partnership at New York Comic Con 2026, where they said the YouTuber has “a few projects in the works” with the studio. “I am proud to announce that I’m working with Blumhouse to launch some new movies. I am taking some of my all-time favorite indie games and horror channels from the interwebs and partnering with Blumhouse to bring them to the big screen,” MatPat said at the panel. The first of these is Amanda the Adventurer, a first-person, puzzle-solving indie horror game that sees the player character unravel an unsettling mystery involving a low-budget animated children’s show of the same name. MatPat announced that he and Blumhouse are currently in talks with writers and directors, saying they’re “actually moving fast” to get this project made. “It’s horror with heart. Amanda is this horrifying but tragic character. It asks the question, ‘Can you trust the media being put in front of your kids?’” he said. This is the latest YouTuber-led film project to hit the news after Sean ‘Jacksepticeye’ McLoughlin revealed he was at the helm of an animated Bloodborne movie . And earlier this year, YouTube star Mark ‘Markiplier’ Fischbach stunned moviegoers with his self-funded horror movie Iron Lung , an adaptation of an indie horror game of the same name. Indie horror games have always had a strong audience online, and it seems that major studios are finally taking notice — especially after the success of Kane Parson’s Backrooms earlier this year. The film was such a hit that other creepypasta movies were greenlit in short order, including adaptations of The Mandela Catalogue , Siren Head , and even The SCP Foundation. Given the viral nature of Amanda the Adventurer, there’s a few good guesses as to what movies MatPat and Blumhouse are cooking up next. Probably all one needs to do is look at CoryxKenshin’s YouTube channel — could a Puppet Combo movie be on the way? (Nun Massacre would be wild to see in a theater.) For more New York Comic Con news, check out our hub of everything major announced at the convention's Marvel panel, as well as a new Avatar: The Last Airbender show and our interview with Daredevil star Charlie Cox.

items.title: Is The Exorcist: Martyrs a Sequel to The Exorcist III? Mike Flanagan Reveals All
items.excerpt: The Exorcist: Martyrs director Mike Flanagan joins IGN to break down the horror sequel's new trailer and explain how it builds on the foundation of The Exorcist III.
items.content_text: There's a lot to be excited about at this year's NYCC, not least of which being the first trailer for Mike Flanagan's The Exorcist: Martyrs . The previous attempt at reinvigorating this iconic horror franchise didn't go so well, but if anyone can turn the ship around, it's the man behind The Haunting of Hill House and the new Carrie series. IGN's Tom Jorgensen was able to sit down with Flanagan and take a deep dive into the trailer. Flanagan breaks down the key characters seen in this new footage and how the film builds on the foundation of the underrated gem that is The Exorcist III. Check out our video interview above or read on to see what he had to say about the film, including the all-important question of whether or not we'll hear "Tubular Bells" in the new film. Tom Jorgensen for IGN: [Let's start with] the first shot of the trailer, which is Scarlett [Johansson] coming down the stairs into that crime scene. Explain why that was the image that you wanted to come right out of the gate with for this trailer. Mike Flanagan: So when we were filming that, we had this incredible location. And I mean, if you're talking about The Exorcist and you have a staircase like that, it's kind of a requirement for a genre like this. That image, I think, not only evokes the descent of Scarlett's character into our story in a really profound way, but is also so evocative to me of the stairs from the original film and of the poster. If you look at the poster for The Exorcist III, check out that poster against that shot. It's kind of wild. IGN: You mentioned The Exorcist III, and you've hinted prior to this that this movie is going to be taking some cues from that sequel. And I think you were maybe understating that a little bit from watching this trailer. What was so appealing about using The Exorcist III as the jumping-off point for this story? Flanagan: The Exorcist III is an awesome movie. It's so underappreciated. Outside of the original, it's my favorite of the franchise. I think it's just a marvelous film. It's terrifying, it's sophisticated, it's beautifully acted. And the thing is that Blatty, both in the novel Legion on which it's based, and then in the film which he directed, is starting to play with the synthesis of two subgenres. And I think that's where I was like, "Aha, what a phenomenal idea. And there's so much we can do to take that idea and run with it." To harmonize a serial killer investigative thriller with the demonic possession story is something that I think that movie first tries to introduce and gives us a chance to truly run with, and that was irresistible. IGN: Yeah, I'll tell you, I figured it was going to be relevant. I had actually not seen The Exorcist III before this weekend, and I just had something itching at me saying it was going to be relevant and that was a good investment of my time. And you're right, the movie is incredible. Flanagan: Great movie. IGN: This trailer is littered with references to the Gemini Killer. We have crucified victims, victims being mutilated in quite specific ways. What is this movie's relationship to the events of The Exorcist III? Do you consider this a direct sequel? Flanagan: Well, it's a tricky question. I think this movie was absolutely designed to stand on its own two feet with people like yourself a week ago who had not seen The Exorcist III. So it is absolutely a self-contained story that is utterly accessible and hopefully thrilling for people who have no knowledge of The Exorcist III, or even frankly of Friedkin's film or Blatty's original novel. It really is its own thing. However, that said, if you are a fan of The Exorcist III, there's just extra bits in here that will delight you. And there is a thread for the super fans to pick up that runs all the way back through the Exorcist III to Friedkin's original for those who are excited by those things. But it was absolutely crafted very intentionally to stand on its own. "There is a thread for the super fans to pick up that runs all the way back through the Exorcist III to Friedkin's original for those who are excited by those things." IGN: Well, I'm going to be one of those people freakishly pulling at those threads for sure. A centerpiece moment of the trailer is Scarlett's character attending the execution of Rivera, who is played by John Leguizamo — incredible casting there by the way — surrounded by hooded executioners. That hood is a motif that recurs throughout the back half of the trailer. What can you tease about Rivera and his significance to this story? Flanagan: Rivera is a serial killer who would leave crime scenes with a very particular religious tableau. Scarlett comes across him very early in the story, and it starts her career as a detective to close that case and to send him away to kind of a final justice. But then elements of that case and of his crime scenes begin to recur in a way that is a bit impossible, that goes beyond what would be possible for a simple copycat. And this case comes back into her life more than a decade later, now that she's a fully established homicide detective and a single mother, and it all kind of comes together. IGN: I'll just say this: I've never paid more attention to which finger of a victim's was severed in a trailer than I have in this trailer right here. We see Scarlett chasing an orange-hooded character out of her house with a gun. Clearly this evil is starting to encroach. Does that theme have a relevance to what you're doing here, the idea of evil coming inside? Flanagan: I think that's kind of at the very heart of every possession story, the incursion of evil onto the human heart, and in this case the human body, into the safety of the family and into innocence itself. That's some of what is fundamentally disturbing about an exorcist story. But the other difference is that the incursion of evil upon society, the incursion of violence upon a civilized world, and how that inspires despair in us when we see the evils of the world and the atrocities with which people can deal with each other — how that despair is something that we can't really escape. And once that infiltrates us, how do you get rid of that? The interesting thing about the synthesis of these two subgenres for me is that typically our protagonists in stories like this react in paralyzed horror to that incursion. Scarlett's character does not have that luxury. She's a homicide detective. She is eye to eye with the greatest horrors that humans can inflict upon each other on a regular basis, and so it is her job — to that scene you're describing in the trailer — to chase down that evil, to run right toward it, to run headfirst into the darkness. [That's] another thing I love about that image of her at the staircase, because that's a moment of observation before you know she's going down there. That's her mission, her job, and it's also who she is, and that makes for a wonderful protagonist that gets to drive this narrative into a lot of places a lot of other possession stories can't go, because there's stories of people running from the darkness, whereas ours is running into it. IGN: It seems like there are also two priests that are going to be allied with Scarlett, very appropriate for The Exorcist, played by Chiwetel Ejiofor and Laurence Fishburne. Holy hell. Flanagan: I know, right? A lot of power in that room. IGN: Excellent voices to be potentially booming some ancient rites. What can you tell us about these two priests? Flanagan: Well, I can tell you Chiwetel plays a character named Father William, who's a prison chaplain, which I think is a fascinating look into a corner of the priesthood that is not really shown before in this franchise or in other Exorcist movies that I could find or think of. When you talk about the level of evil we're dealing with — and I've said before, I truly believe this is the scariest movie I've ever gotten to work on by quite a lot — there's a profound darkness. There's an epistle darkness at the heart of this story and it is vicious. This is a story about the fight against that kind of darkness. And if you're going to be depicting that fight, you need fighters of a certain weight. And when you talk about Laurence Fishburne, this is someone who carries that weight with him the second he steps into a room in a way that is pretty profound. So yeah, there's a bit of a heavyweight matchup here. IGN: I think my favorite performance of Chiwetel Ejiofor's ever is actually The Operative in Serenity, that almost religious, dogmatic appreciation for something. Was that role at all on your mind when you cast him? Flanagan: Oh, I love that movie so much. I geeked out on him when we did Life of Chuck about Serenity, and particularly there's one line in this beautiful high-angle shot at the end where he says, "There's nothing left to see." It's a haunting sign-off for this true believer that is so misguided. It's a wonderful character. But yeah, I think Chiwetel's an extraordinary actor, one of the best I've ever worked with. And that's why after we did Life of Chuck, I was determined to work with him again. But this part lets him do a number of things that'll be very surprising. IGN: Cannot wait to see it. Flanagan: Yeah, it's a wonderful role for him and I think one of my favorite of his performances. IGN: There's this really excellent image that I loved of this bloody barrel in that abandoned mall. It gets paid off later in very gory fashion. What do you notice most about how both The Exorcist and The Exorcist III evoke terror, and how do you go about honoring that in this movie with imagery like that? Flanagan: Well, I think the thing that terrified me the most about The Exorcist — and there are visceral scares throughout, images, sounds, things that hit you on this primal level — isn't the rotating heads or the vomit or the levitation. The thing that scares me about The Exorcist is that it paints a portrait of a world where Satan is clearly real and active and God seems nowhere to be found. And that chills me. There's no safety net. It's a world where innocent children can die horribly and no God will intervene on their behalf, which coincidentally is the world we live in. I think that is at its heart what makes it so upsetting, and I think where these films and the books especially tap into something that I think really affects people is that it roots this in a perversion of religious iconography. It takes things that are meant to be sacred and makes them a sacrilege. That barrel, if you have a certain level of knowledge of the method of death of Catholic saints and martyrs, means something and it's a twisted perversion of something that is holy in the church. As someone who was raised Catholic and who was horrified and fascinated by martyrdom and by the method of death of so many Catholic saints — which are, I have to say, some of the worst ways you can imagine a human being dying in a lot of cases — to imagine a mockery of that where there appears to be no safety net and no intervention from anything good regardless of the nature of the victim made the story horrifying to me. That's what terrifies me about it. There's scares, there's imagery, there's all sorts of stuff that's truly unsettling, but the thing that unsettles me the most is unchecked evil in the human world that there appears to be no remedy for. That to me is just horrifying. IGN: On the way out the door: "Tubular Bells," yes or no? Flanagan: No! For more, check out IGN's review of the Carrie series and our full breakdown of the show's ending .
items.title_en: Is The Exorcist: Martyrs a Sequel to The Exorcist III? Mike Flanagan Reveals All

items.title: A Street Fighter Movie Sequel Is Already Being Written, but There’s a Catch
items.excerpt: Director Kitao Sakurai confirmed that he’s already hard at work writing up a sequel to his upcoming Street Fighter film, but whether or not it gets made all depends on how the first movie performs.
items.content_text: Director Kitao Sakurai confirmed that he’s already hard at work writing up a sequel to his upcoming Street Fighter film, but whether or not it gets made all depends on how the first movie performs. Sakurai spoke about the possibility of a sequel in an interview with MovieWeb , saying the groundwork is already being laid to continue Ryu and Ken’s adventures after the events of the second World Warrior Tournament. But if fans want to see their fights continue after this, they’ll have to put their butts in some seats at their local theaters to make it happen. “It's something that we're thinking about and developing,” he told the outlet. “I don't want to say anything that locks us in. It also kind of depends on how people react to this one, and whether they, you know, support this vision of the story. We definitely have a lot of ideas, and we're writing currently, but you know, I wouldn't want to make any promises one way or the other about what exactly we're gonna do." Having spoken with the cast myself, I can confirm that their hopes for a sequel are high, but they’ve also confirmed that interest from moviegoers is essential in order to justify making another Street Fighter film. Just today, it was confirmed that the Street Fighter movie will contain several animated sequences diving into Ryu and Ken’s backstory with their mentor, Gouken, and his brother, Akuma. Fans are already providing positive feedback to what they’ve seen so far, praising the art style and fluid animation — but there’s one character who’s been left out of the marketing thus far, and he’s already getting the community’s gears turning as to who a sequel might be about. We haven’t yet seen Sagat in any of the film's trailers or advertisements, and no casting announcements have been made for him. Obviously, fans are hopeful that, if a sequel does end up getting made, Sagat will be a significant part of it — but given the wealth of characters in Street Fighter games , there’s no telling who might show up in a second movie. This is the second big film from Capcom to hit theaters following Zach Cregger's Resident Evil adaptation, which was broadly well-received by regular moviegoers and critics, alike, though hopes for a sequel are also low at the moment, given that Cregger has publicly claimed he will "never" touch a franchise film again. Street Fighter releases in theaters on October 16, 2026. We got the chance to speak to the cast ahead of its release, including David Dastmalchian, who told us all about how he studied real-life cult leaders to bring M. Bison to the big screen.
items.title_en: A Street Fighter Movie Sequel Is Already Being Written, but There’s a Catch

items.title: Magic: The Gathering at NYCC Live Blog – Get Ready For Darkhold Destiny
items.excerpt: Earlier this year at MagicCon in Las Vegas, Wizards of the Coast revealed its in-universe sets for 2027, but that only covered three of the six planned sets. The other three are Universes Beyond — the card game's crossover brand — and now we know about another one, Darkhold Destiny, the new Marvel set.
items.content_text: Earlier this year at MagicCon in Las Vegas, Wizards of the Coast revealed its in-universe sets for 2027, but that only covered three of the six planned sets. The other three are Universes Beyond — the card game's crossover brand — and now we know about another one, Darkhold Destiny, the new Marvel set. Wizards of the Coast and Marvel teased Darkhold Destiny in a YouTube video, and while we still don't know what cards or mechanics are in the set, I've seen some of the art, and it looks incredible, and a much better fit for Magic's aesthetic. Hopefully, in the MTG panel at NYCC, they'll dive into more detail on what the set actually is. Unfortunately the panel will not be streamed, but I'll be there live, reporting all the details on what Wizards of the Coast and Marvel have been cooking up since the Marvel Superheroes set back in June. The two Marvel UB sets have been mixed, with the Spider-Man set being a major let down, while Marvel Superheroes had a ton of great cards and a fun limited environment. Let's just hope Darkhold Destiny is a much better set. But from the early art in the teaser, I'm starting to get my hopes up. The panel starts at 7:45 pm ET / 4:45 pm PT, so we at least won't have to wait long to see what's in store. Magic The Gathing x Marvel @ NYCC Live Blog All times are in EST 8:35 pm: And that's the show. Darkhold Destiny, looks like a cool set, but there's still a lot that Wizards didn't reveal. But it's a decent start! 8:33 pm: WotC announced a special promo or Doctor Doom, King of Latveria for Avengers Doomsday. you'll be able to grab it if you go see the movie at a Regal Cinemas on opening weekend "as long as supplies last". It's the face of the Dr. Doom commander deck, and it's done in the style of the MCU, so I expect it'll go fast. 8:31 pm: One more thing. There will be three Secret Lair drops inspired by Dr. Doom, just in time for the new Avengers movie. They're not revealing which cards are in the drop yet, but there is Dr. Doom art, and they told the crowd "you'll have to guess which reprint this is". I guess we'll wait. 8:26 pm: There are new Secret Lair, a countdown kit, a giant box with 30 cards. This thing is about to cost a lot of money. Most people will get it in nonfoil, but there will be a random chance that you'll get it in traditional foil, and an even more rare chance to get it in surge foil. I guess the Secret Lair booster packs didn't work, but we're at least getting to gamble on whether or not they're foil. The Secret Lair launches November 2nd. 8:22 pm: There will be two bundles, a regular bundle and an 'Arcanum' bundle. Both of these will have their own mechanically unique promo card. Hopefully that card doesn't get too expensive! There are also two scene boxes, also filled with mechanically unique cards. 8:19 pm: For the product suite, we have Booster Packs, Collector Boosters, Prerelease Pack and Draft Night (which also has a Collector Booster). There will also be four commander decks, Strange Academy (WUB), Gods of Asgard (RGW), Midnight Sons (WB) and Lords of Hel (BR). There will also be Collectors Editions for each deck that'll be completely decked out in surge foils. 8:16 pm: The basic lands take after the Adventures From the Forgotten Realms lands, with flavor text that tell the story. Unlike that D&D set, though, each Basic Land type has two variants, one before Hela and Dormammu's invasion and one after. They look awesome. 8:13 pm: One more card, Temple of Khonshu. It's a common black/white land and it enters tapped unless you control a Dimension. Dimension is some kind of new card type, and Wizards is not revealing it yet. I hope they're better than Battles. 8:10 pm: They brought Arcane back, which was a card subtype that hasn't really existed since the Kamigawa block in the 2000s. We got a black modal spell, and a red one "Rise From the Nether" that creates 3/1 creature tokens. Bring back Splice Onto Arcane. 8:08 pm: Hela's card looks awesome, it introduces a new keyword, Vengeance, which is basically just an Adventure that you cast when the card is in the graveyard. So, if Hela is your commander, you can send her to the graveyard when she dies, then put her in the command zone when you cast from the graveyard, and make a little loop. 8:05 pm: They introduced Magik as a dual faced card. WotC didn't add all the X-Men, but Magik fits the vibe of the set, and she looks awesome. She'll be able to transform into Darkchild, and you'll be able to pay 4 life to give her indestructible. So, she'll be pretty hard to kill. 8:03 pm: But even with all the art, there has to be cards. The centerpiece is The Darkhold, a legendary artifact for three mana, and you can tap it, put sin counters on it and draw a card for each sin counter. It's like an evil version of The One Ring. 8:01 pm: The set will be themed around three different types of magic. Arcane for Doctor Strange & Co, Divine for gods like Thor and Dark Magic for villains like Hela and Dormammu. But there are some heroes might be using Dark Magic. 7:57 pm: Once they got the greenlight, WotC had to invent a lot, apparently. The first two sets were about superheroes, but with Darkhold Destiny, the company was much more interested in focusing on villains. So, we've got Hela has a foil to Thor, and the Dread Dormammu as the foil to Doctor Strange. Hela x Dormammu is quite a cool team-up, I'm not going to lie. 7:53 pm: The main heroes of the set are Doctor Strange and Thor, which perfectly fit the theme of the set. And it's not Thor as the Avenger, it's Thor as a god. It sounds like the story really came together after Magic designers pitched their idea for a darker Marvel world. 7:52 pm: There will be new crossover comics, coming out via Infinity Comics. The first issue will be out in February, with another coming closer to the April release. That should introduce people to the world that Marvel and WotC have been building together. 7:50 pm: Now they're showing off some of the art, and it looks just like something out of Innistrad. Ok, well maybe not exactly Innistrad, but very similar vibes. 7:49 pm: Marvel and Wizards have been working on this set together for years. Marvel Super Heroes and Spider-Man it was focused on just getting everyone's favorite characters in the game, but Darkhold Destiny is focused more on world-building. The World was the focus, and then WotC added characters that would fit later. 7:47 pm: Darkhold Destiny is out April 8, will be the second set next year, after Nauctis. Moon Knight, Ghost Rider, Blade will all be here, along with traditional MTG creature types like elves, dragons, angels and vampires. 7:43 pm: They're starting things off by playing the teaser Wizards released earlier today. They created a whole new Marvel narrative that's unique to Magic: the Gathering. As soon as the teaser was over, the room exploded in cheers. 7:40 pm: Mark Rosewater & Co have taken the stage, and Rosewater is wearing a blue Marvel shirt. And they've also dragged a replica of the Darkhold onto the stage. Here we go! 7:27 pm: Now, with Darkhold Destiny, that makes for the third Marvel set. The first two have each had one of the Infinity Stones, so it's extremely likely that the third will be in this one. I wonder which one it'll be! 7:17 pm: Got to the panel, and it looks like they opened the doors early! The room is absolutely packed, and people seem excited to see more of Darkhold Destiny. We've got about 30 mintues to go before the show kicks off. 6:15 pm: I'm about to head over to the panel, but it looks like Wizards of the Coast has already announced the new set on YouTube . It's Darkhold Destiny, and it looks like a completely original take on Marvel. None of the cards or mechanics have been announced, but this fits Magic's world much better than Spider-Man or Marvel Superheroes did.

items.title: The Oregon Coast Aquarium Has Now Named Multiple Octopuses After Dungeon Crawler Carl Characters
items.excerpt: The influence of Dungeon Crawler Carl has officially reached the animal kingdom. The Oregon Coast Aquarium just welcomed a new giant Pacific Octopus and named it after a certain changeling that fans of the series will recognize: Juicebox.
items.content_text: The influence of Dungeon Crawler Carl has officially reached the animal kingdom. The Oregon Coast Aquarium just welcomed a new giant Pacific Octopus and named it after a certain changeling that fans of the series will recognize: Juicebox. While it's certainly interesting that Matt Dinniman's characters have already taken root in my local aquarium, according to the report from Oregon Live , this is actually the second Octopus to get named after DCC. Juicebox will be sharing the aquarium with a 22.5-pound male Octopus called Donut, after Princess Donut herself. The aquarists who chose Juicebox's name told Oregon Live it was because of octopuses' inherent ability to change their appearance to blend in. For those not familiar with the books, Juicebox is a changeling that is able to shift into various forms at will. For additional context (and minor spoiler!), Juicebox does shift into Ursula from The Little Mermaid at one point in the story, so the transition to an octopus isn't that big of a stretch. Juicebox the Octopus is now available to visit at the Oregon Coast Aquarium in Newport and will stay there for about a year before being released back to the reef. As someone who has regularly visited that aquarium, I can attest to the quality of their Octopus Den. And as a fan of the Dungeon Crawler Carl books , this little tidbit of news is a great excuse to go back and visit again. Naming an octopus after a character from a popular franchise is certainly just a marketing stunt to get more people to visit the aquarium, but that doesn't make it any less impactful. The fact that Juicebox got added to the aquarium just as another octopus named Anakin was released just makes it even better. Will Dungeon Crawler Carl ever be as big as Star Wars? Probably not, but the octopus trends seem to be heading in that direction. The sudden rise from popular LitRPG book series to octopus fame is par for the course for Dungeon Crawler Carl in 2026. This year alone, the eighth book is coming out — along with tabletop games and an entire toy line — and a TV adaptation was confirmed at Peacock with Seth McFarlane in charge.

items.title: Gears of War: E-Day Estimated Sales Reach Just 230,000 in First Week, Analyst Says
items.excerpt: Xbox console exclusive Gears of War: E-Day is reportedly off to a soft start after reaching an estimated 230,000 copies sold in its first week.
items.content_text: Xbox console exclusive Gears of War: E-Day is reportedly off to a soft start after reaching an estimated 230,000 copies sold in its first week. The alleged sales update arrived from Alinea Analytics' head of marketing analysis, Rhys Elliott, who shared early data for the Gears prequel on X/Twitter. After arriving via early access last week (its full launch arrived this past Tuesday), Gears of War: E-Day has reportedly moved just 230,000 copies across PC and Xbox devices. Steam sales account for 168,000 of that number, with Xbox sales, including both console and PC, totaling just 62,000. These numbers, which are unofficial figures that have not been backed by Microsoft in any official capacity and should be taken with a grain of salt, are low for the game leading the charge on Xbox's refocus toward exclusive games, as players shift their attention from purchasing the base experience to dipping their toes in with Game Pass. Game Pass is seemingly to blame for its performance related to raw copies sold on Xbox-supported devices, with Elliott saying the subscription service is "cannibalising much of the premium revenue." While that's not to say Gears of War: E-Day is having trouble garnering attention – Alinea estimated that 1.7 million players have accessed the game via Game Pass – the data does suggest that players are far more interested in access through their subscriptions rather than outright owning a copy. Of the nearly 2 million to launch Gears of War: E-Day through Game Pass, 722,000 users are believed to have paid the extra $30 to upgrade to its Premium Edition to unlock early access. Revenue earned through the Xbox ecosystem reportedly amounted to $27 million, with total earnings reaching about $37 million. How exactly Gears of War: E-Day may have factored into revenue earned through new and returning Game Pass subscriptions is currently unclear. "While E-Day is a sublime game (it's made my top 10), these are soft numbers for a flagship when Xbox badly needs revenue wins," Elliott said. "E-Day sold 62K copies on Xbox against 722K Premium upgrades, so for every one copy sold on Xbox, nearly 12 Game Pass upgrades were sold. The $70 premium SKU is – functionally – dead on Xbox. In a world without day-one Game Pass, many of these folks would have bought E-Day at $70. They paid $30 for five days early access to something they don’t own. Xbox is, in effect, charging its most valuable customers the least, based on a hangover from a tried-and-exhausted strategy from a previous administration." The idea that Game Pass has negatively affected standalone sales is something Microsoft has seemingly been internally aware of before, with 2023 documents related to the Activision Blizzard merger noting a decline in base game sales in the first year after a title is added to the service. The Xbox company told IGN at the time that the model "offers gamers and game creators more choice and opportunity in how they discover, experience, and deliver games." While Microsoft has yet to confirm official sales data, and it's unclear how Gears of War: E-Day may have driven new Game Pass subscriptions, slow sales could sour an otherwise successful launch. The Marcus Fenix and Dom Santiago-led prequel emerged with strong reviews from both fans and critics, with IGN's early review, which covered only the campaign mode, awarding a 9/10 . Earlier this week, The Coalition studio head Mike Crump said Gears of War: E-Day is a "natural choice to be" an Xbox exclusive . He also addressed concerns around potential layoffs at the studio , while promising that the next installment in the series won't take nearly as long to make.
items.title_en: Gears of War: E-Day Estimated Sales Reach Just 230,000 in First Week, Analyst Says

items.title: Turok the Dinosaur Hunter Returns for Skybound Visions Imprint - NYCC 2026
items.excerpt: Iconic dinosaur hunter Turok is finally making a comeback in 2027, as Skybound kicks off an ambitious new imprint dubbed Skybound Visions.
items.content_text: Fans of the iconic dinosaur hunter Turok will be pleased to know the character is making a big comeback at Skybound in 2027. As announced at NYCC, the company is kicking off a new creator-focused imprint called Skybound Visions, one that launches with a Turok: Son of Stone comic and new additions to the Transformers and G.I. Joe franchises. Skybound Visions is intended to offer standalone stories focused on creators reinventing popular characters in bold and unexpected ways. Case in point, Turok: Son of Stone reboots the character under The Buffalo Hunter Hunter writer Stephen Graham Jones and The Old Guard artist Leandro Fernández. “Skybound Visions pairs beloved comic book characters with the most interesting comic book creators working today, to present their personal takes on these fan-favorites,” said Sean Mackiewicz, SVP, Skybound, in a statement. “Visions is all about surprising creators, surprising characters, and surprising storytelling, and we have plenty more in store for 2027 and beyond." Read on to learn more about all three of the inaugural Skybound Visions titles and see early previews of each one. Transformers: Bumblebee - Lost Planet Creative Team: Tate Brombal & Matt Emmons Release Date: January 27, 2027 After a devastating Decepticon attack, Bumblebee is stranded on an uncharted planet. Lost in the galaxy, with no way to call for help, the so-called “weakest of all the Autobots” must tackle the biggest mission of his young life. But beneath its surface, this strange planet holds a secret that’s already begun to corrupt and change its indigenous life. Now, the Autobots’ greatest hope must come from the evolution of its most unexpected warrior... if Bee can survive being hunted by the deadliest Decepticon of all! G.I. Joe: The Island of Dr. Mindbender Creative Team: Karl Kerschl & Doug Mahnke Release Date: February 2, 2027 The last team of Joes sent to the Island of Dr. Mindbender never came back… Now, Codename: Flint must return to active duty to lead a fresh batch of recruits to the isolated compound of a madman. A mad scientist who’s grown madder every year--and his creations more monstrous. In the deadliest mission of his career, Flint just wants to rescue his old friends and get back to his family. But on this island, survival isn’t just half the battle--it's the whole damn war! Turok: Son of Stone Creative Team: Stephen Graham Jones & Leandro Fernández Release Date: March 10, 2027 Turok wanted to dig up the past. Now, he must survive it. Turok dreamed that his dig in New Mexico would make his name legendary. But when the ground gave way, he fell through history and landed in a valley that shouldn’t exist. Where the Ice Age sits on top of the time of dinosaurs, and at every turn he discovers an era older and hungrier than the last. In a relentless quest to return to his son, Turok must unearth the truth about this hidden world and not lose his grip on a shifting reality that threatens to consume him. Sometimes a dream coming true is a nightmare beyond imagination… You can preorder all three Skybound Visions titles at your local comic shop . In other NYCC news, we got an exclusive first look at Mattel's first DC Premium figure , and we also got hands-on time with the new Marvel Webtoon app . Jesse is a mild-mannered staff writer for IGN. items.title: The Street Fighter 2 Bonus Stage Car Is Real and You Can Win It
items.excerpt: The General is teaming up with Capcom to bring the destroyable car from Street Fighter II to life, and you have a chance to win it — along with more than $25,000 in gas money.
items.content_text: The General is teaming up with Capcom to bring the destroyable car from Street Fighter II to life, and you have a chance to win it — along with more than $25,000 in gas money. Street Fighter II’s iconic bonus stage lets players beat the literal brakes off of a Lexus LS 400. It’s a feature that’s stayed with the series throughout the years, challenging fighting game fans to beat it to a pulp within a certain time limit. It’s even referenced in the upcoming Street Fighter movie, with trailers showing Noah Centineo’s Ken Masters punching and kicking a car to bits while surrounded by a crowd of adoring fans. More than 30 years later, this car is coming to the real world, thanks to a joint collaboration between The General Insurance (yes, that General), Capcom, and Vehicle Effects, a Los Angeles-based company that makes custom rides of all sorts, many of which have been featured in films and TV shows. Vehicle Effects has made a recreation of the pixelated Lexus from Street Fighter II — though we don’t recommend you actually destroy it if you end up winning it in their sweepstakes. Starting in October, fans have until November 18 to enter the sweepstakes for a chance at snagging the car for themselves, as well as $25,400.69 (nice) in gas money. And hey, it’s a pretty good car; as pointed out by Eventhubs , the Lexus LS 400 is widely considered to be one of the most “overengineered” cars of all time, with a 4.0-liter V8 engine that’s been nicknamed the "million-mile engine.” (It’s the only thing left behind after you destroy it in the bonus stage, after all.) On top of its pixelated paint job and upgraded sound system, the words “you” and “win” are emblazoned on both the driver’s side and passenger side headrests, and you can even insert a literal coin to activate its accompanying seat warmers. It’s hard to kick butt when you’ve got cold glutes, after all. The Street Fighter movie releases in theaters on October 16, 2026. Just today, it was revealed that the movie will feature animated segments diving into Ryu and Ken’s backstory with their master, Gouken, and Akuma. We got the chance to speak to the cast of the film ahead of time, including David Dastmachian, who told us all about how he studied real-life cult leaders to bring M. Bison to the big screen . items.title: Marvel Comics Reveals New Captain Marvel Series and Daredevil #700 - NYCC 2026
items.excerpt: Marvel dropped some big announcements at NYCC, including Daredevil #700 and a brand-new Captain Marvel series from Kamala Khan co-creator G. Willow Wilson.
items.content_text: Marvel Comics made some big announcements during the publisher's "Bullpen Bulletins! With Stephen Wacker" panel. The newly minted editor-in-chief revealed several big projects for early 2027, including a brand-new ongoing Captain Marvel series and the milestone issue Daredevil #700. The new volume of Captain Marvel will be written by G. Willow Wilson, whom Marvel fans will best remember as the co-creator of current Ms. Marvel Kamala Khan. This time, Wilson is turning her attention to Kamala's mentor, Carol Danvers, who is facing a dark new status quo following the destructive events of Avengers: Armageddon . Captain Marvel will be illustrated by Rachael Stott (Fantastic Four). Here's the official summary for the series: Following the cataclysmic events of Avengers: Armageddon, Carol Danvers finds herself grounded like never before. To rise again, Carol will have to challenge everything she thought she knew about being Captain Marvel—and break every rule along the way. And as she pushes herself further, a threat that has been quietly assembling in the shadows of the Marvel Universe for decades is finally ready to make its move. Look for Captain Marvel #1 to debut in May 2027. As for Daredevil, the series will reach its 700th issue in March 2027. That oversized issue will feature a main story by regular series writer Stephanie Phillips and artist Lee Garbett, along with a new cover by Daredevil veteran David Mack. Also during the panel, Marvel teased the climactic finale of a major Uncanny X-Men storyline called "Soul Deep," as well as a spinoff miniseries called X-Men: Regulators. Regulators is written by Mikki Kendall and drawn by Georges Jeanty and will debut in February 2027. items.content_text: Bill Murray has reprised the role of Dr. Peter Venkman in a new advertisement for Rivian electric vehicles that sees the original Ghostbuster respond to a call of Slimer terrorizing a suburban house by pulling up in the "Ecto-R1," aka a Rivian R1S SUV decked out like the original Ecto-1 ambulance/hearse. The 70-second spot shows off the special new Ghostbusters-themed Halloween software update for the R1S, R1T pickup truck, and new R2 SUV. In it, Rivian owners can play with a Ghostbusters UI on the cars' main center touchscreen display, play "'Mallow Mash" on the screen by squashing the Mini-Pufts flying around, plus hidden Easter eggs to discover. The update also adds custom sounds, a Slimer settings theme, a Trick or Treat Mode that can detect and greet costumed guests with Ghostbusters sound effects and lights, and custom themes for the exterior light bars, cabin lights, and overhead lights such as Proton Pack and Ghost Trap. The Ghostbusters Halloween theme will be available in Rivians from today through November 2. Rivian launched its highly anticipated R2 earlier this year to great reviews. It keeps a very similiar design as the lauded R1S but shrinks both the size and the price. The R2's base price is $45,000, though in this current early stage of production, only the maxed-out, tri-motor, fully loaded Performance model is available for a starting price of $58,000. Murray last played Dr. Venkman in 2024's Ghosbusters: Frozen Empire, which IGN's reviewer did not care for . The last Ghostbusters video game was 2022's Ghostbusters, Spirits Unleashed, an asymmetrical multiplayer game our reviewer thought was OK .

items.title: Lucasfilm Games Producer Responds After Galactic Racer Character Biddy Blas Goes Viral
items.excerpt: If you’ve been on gaming Twitter recently, you’ve probably seen a clip from Star Wars: Galactic Racer making the rounds on your timeline — specifically, a player’s interaction with a character named Biddy Blas.
items.content_text: If you’ve been on gaming Twitter recently, you’ve probably seen a clip from Star Wars: Galactic Racer making the rounds on your timeline — specifically, a player’s interaction with a character named Biddy Blas. It’s almost impossible to hate the guy, who tells you all about how awesome he is in a hilarious spiel that has somehow become everyone’s new vocal stim. In Huttese, Blas tells you: “Here’s a name for you, amateur! Biddy Blas. Write it down. items.title: Is Marvel's Zodiac Actually an Agents of SHIELD Revival?
items.excerpt: The Marvel Cinematic Universe is expanding once again, because Marvel Studios has announced at New York Comic Con a new “spy thriller” called Zodiac. But could this actually be an Agents of SHIELD revival?
items.content_text: The Marvel Cinematic Universe is expanding once again, because Marvel Studios has announced at New York Comic Con another project that will debut after Avengers: Secret Wars wraps up the Multiverse Saga. That would be Zodiac , a new “spy thriller” from Marvel Television. But besides a 2028 release window, we don’t have any other official information beyond the show’s logo, which has resulted in Marvel fans the world over asking the question: What the heck is this show even about? Is it a character? An organization? Is Marvel making a TV series about the Zodiac Killer? (Not likely on that last one). Meanwhile, Clark Gregg, aka Agent Phil Coulson from Agents of SHIELD , seems excited about the new show... or at least has shared the Zodiac news on social media. Hmm... Well, Zodiac does in fact exist in the Marvel comics universe as a team of villains. So let’s look at the source material and other MCU projects to see if we can figure out what Marvel has up their sleeve... and whether or not this means Agents of SHIELD could somehow be returning too. Marvel's Zodiac Cartel Explained The most prominent Zodiac in the Marvel universe is the Zodiac Cartel, a group of 12 supervillains who stylize themselves after the signs of Western astrology. So there’s someone named Aries, someone named Taurus, someone named Gemini... you get the idea. The organization is a subversive criminal group who sought world domination under the leadership of Cornelius van Lunt, aka Taurus, and would become recurring enemies of the Avengers. Although they made several appearances over the years, the Zodiac Cartel has never been a standout member of the Avengers’ rogues gallery – they’re not exactly on the same level as Loki, Ultron, or Thanos. Their schemes often involve the Zodiac Key, a powerful cosmic artifact that can generate psionic energy and empower mechanical devices. One of the most notable aspects of the Zodiac Cartel is that Scorpio’s alter ego is Jake Fury, the brother of SHIELD director Nick Fury. While the original Zodiac stories had Jake as a villain who came into conflict with SHIELD and the Avengers, later stories in the Secret Warriors comic would reveal that the evil Jake was actually a Life Model Decoy (basically a robot that mimics a specific person), and the real Jake had been secretly helping his brother all along. The storyline in Secret Warriors also featured the Great Wheel, a version of the Zodiac group founded by none other than Leonardo da Vinci, which may be what's referenced in the "O" in the Zodiac show's logo. Several other evil groups took up the Zodiac name after the first Cartel, including one composed entirely of Life Model Decoys, but none made much of an impact. Zodiac as a concept has struggled to break out in the Marvel comics universe, with other nefarious groups like Hydra, Advanced Idea Mechanics, and the Hand being much more popular. Is Agents of SHIELD Being Revived? Since Zodiac isn’t a well-known aspect of the Marvel universe, it’s surprising to see Marvel Studios greenlight a show named after them. It feels more likely that Marvel will reinvent the idea instead of doing a straightforward adaptation of the Zodiac Cartel – I doubt we’ll see van Lunt decked out in a bull costume. Since Hydra seems to be defunct in the MCU, and given that Marvel described the show as a spy thriller, perhaps Zodiac will be established as a new evil espionage group working in the shadows as part of the MCU’s next saga. This would make sense given that the “A” in the Zodiac logo looks quite similar to the eagle emblem used for SHIELD in the MCU. Which raises our next question: Is Zodiac actually an Agents of SHIELD revival? That would track with Clark Gregg, who plays Phil Coulson in the MCU, sharing the Zodiac announcement on social media. Will the show feature the return of Agent Coulson? What about Chloe Bennet’s Quake or Ming-Na Wen’s Melinda May? It’s been a while since we’ve seen them, but the Agents of SHIELD characters making a comeback would be a welcome development for the MCU. Given that Zodiac has ties to SHIELD in the comics, this feels like the perfect place for the Agents of SHIELD characters to return to the fold. Agents of SHIELD is one of the holdouts from the pre-Disney+ era of Marvel television that hasn’t been reintegrated into the shared universe. Although Marvel Television insisted that “it’s all connected” back in the day, Coulson’s SHIELD team hasn’t been brought back in new MCU projects in the same way Daredevil and friends have. However, given that Zodiac has ties to SHIELD in the comics and the SHIELD insignia is referenced in the show’s logo, this feels like the perfect place for those characters to return to the fold. Perhaps Coulson’s team has to reunite to deal with a new threat in whatever form the MCU’s Zodiac organization takes. Maybe Samuel L. Jackson, who recently confirmed he will return as Nick Fury for Avengers: Secret Wars, will appear in Zodiac if they pursue the Jake Fury storyline. Of course, we’d be remiss not to mention that Zodiac does already exist in one way in the MCU… What About the Zodiac Bioweapon From Agent Carter? So this is a deep cut even by MCU standards, but Marvel made a handful of short films called Marvel One-Shots in the MCU’s early days. One of those was Agent Carter in 2013, a precursor to the television show of the same name starring Hayley Atwell’s Peggy Carter. In the short, which takes place after Steve Rogers went into the ice at the end of Captain America: The First Avenger, Peggy takes it upon herself to retrieve a blue vial from some criminals. This vial contains a bioweapon codenamed Zodiac, and while the short ends with Zodiac safely back in the good guys’ hands, it hasn’t been followed up on in later MCU projects. Could this bioweapon be what the bad guys are after in the Zodiac show? We don’t know, but it wouldn’t be the first time Marvel has picked up dangling plot threads many years down the line. Hopefully it works out better than the Leader’s appearance in Captain America: Brave New World! What do you think Marvel’s Zodiac is about? Let us know in the comments! Carlos Morales writes novels, articles, and Mass Effect essays. You can follow his fixations on Twitter .

items.title: Skate Developer Promises More Creative Tools Are Coming After ReSkate Modding Platform Goes Viral
items.excerpt: Full Circle, the developer of Skate, published a statement addressing community mods following the viral launch of a fan-made modding platform called ReSkate.
items.content_text: Full Circle, the developer of Skate, published a statement addressing community mods following the viral launch of a fan-made modding platform called ReSkate. ReSkate was officially released into the wild about a week ago. This platform allows fans to play the game offline, create private servers, make their own maps, and more. It’s already been downloaded over 350,000 times on GitHub, and its creators are well-aware that they might get hit with a cease-and-desist order. However, that doesn’t seem to be a problem — at least, not yet, but the devs at Full Circle are keeping an eye on the situation. Full Circle published a statement acknowledging fan mods on October 9, where they admitted to the importance of community mods, while also standing firm against those that bypass paid cosmetics or make money off of new features. “Skateboarding in general is built on community and creative expression, and we support that. We love seeing your passion for pushing the limits of San Vansterdam in different ways. That's why we built our new skateboarding sandbox in San Vansterdam to begin with, to give you, the players, the tools you need to have fun and create amazing content,” it wrote. “To be completely clear, we are not against creativity from players or stopping that from happening. Where we have to draw the line is when mods or other tools bypass our systems to unlock paid cosmetics, release gated/unreleased content, or profit from these unauthorized assets. That rips off the artists, skate brands, and creators, as well as our own development team here at Full Circle, who work hard to bring skate culture into our game." Full Circle went on to confirm that it is aware that players want “more freedom and custom features,” and revealed that it’s currently building “official, secure access tools that enable broader, deeper community creation.” More news on this will be shared at a later date. A message from the team at Full Circle regarding mods and community content. https://t.co/sTiTUvkRWX — skate. (@skate) October 9, 2026 ReSkate’s popularity is undeniable; after its release, Skate’s playerbase saw a massive jump in active players, peaking at over 7,000 players on October 5 — the highest it’s been for months after the game's launch in September 2025. Speaking with PC Gamer , the developers of ReSkate admitted that they “honestly didn't realize how big this was going to be," saying they were “just doing it for the love of the game." They also told the outlet that they are prepared to take ReSkate down if EA’s lawyers come knocking, which many fans are already assuming will happen at some point down the line. For now, though, ReSkate remains alive and well, and it has seemingly spurred Full Circle into taking action to give the game more community-friendly features.
